title: fix(sse): streaming partial-JSON delimiter + token/event ordering for OpenAI compat
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: downstream SDKs and third-party consumers using the OpenAI-compatible SSE stream observed intermittent JSON parse errors for partial-JSON responses and tool/function-calling payloads. Root cause: the SSE encoder was emitting delimiter tokens (data: <json chunk>

) and token/event sentinel frames in an ordering that allowed partial JSON messages and token event frames to interleave such that the consumer received a JSON fragment followed by a token/event boundary or trailing delimiter that produced malformed partial JSON slices. This PR: 1) reorders emission so delimiter/frame boundaries are always emitted after payload bytes are flushed, preventing trailing sentinel tokens from splitting JSON fields; 2) introduces an explicit partial-json sentinel and enforces that partial-json chunks are only cut on safe boundaries (string/escape-aware, not simply buffer boundaries); 3) updates the token/event framing to always emit token-event metadata as a separate SSE event after the current 'data:' JSON chunk completes, guaranteeing consumer-side ordering; 4) adds a compatibility shim in the OpenAI-compat layer that accepts both legacy delimiter ordering and the new strict ordering during a grace period to avoid breaking existing clients; 5) improves unit and integration tests (node/python SDKs and internal streaming harness) with long-run fuzzing to reproduce delimiter/token reorder issues; 6) adds a runtime feature flag to enable the strict ordering immediately for new customers and a staged rollout for existing tenants. Implementation notes: changes in runtime/sse/encoder.go implement string-aware chunking and add metadata to track safe cut points; runtime/sse/streamer.go changes ensure flush-and-emit ordering; openai/compat/stream_decoder.ts contains the shim and transition logic. Testing and rollout: added deterministic unit tests and 2 new e2e test suites in perf-canary that validate token ordering with function-calling outputs and large JSON objects, CI flakiness fixed by stabilizing test network timing; canary rollout started for 10% of hosted API traffic with feature-flag and monitor dashboards created in Redwood Console (SSE stream error rate, parse errors by customer, latency impact). Backwards compatibility: shim retains support for older ordering for 30 days then logs deprecation warnings to customers using legacy behavior. See checklist below.
commits: fix(sse): reorder delimiter emission and add safe-cut chunker
test(sse): add fuzz regression tests for partial JSON and token ordering
chore(openai-compat): add shim and transition flag
docs(sse): add notes about partial-json sentinel and rollout
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Found a race in streamer.flush() where notifier could run before bytes were pushed; requested explicit flush+await ordering.
Priya Nair: Please add a test that simulates backpressure from slow consumers; added a follow-up test in sdk-node.
Mateo Ruiz: Verified OpenAI compat shim for older delimiter ordering; asked for metrics to detect legacy clients.
Ava Martinez: Addressed flush race and added backpressure test. Added metrics (sse.parse_errors_by_client) and a migration plan in rollout notes.
ci_checks: integration/sse-e2e: pass (rerun once due to network flakiness)
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming partial-JSON delimiter and token/event ordering to prevent downstream JSON parse errors. Includes OpenAI-compat shim and staged rollout. No breaking changes expected.
rollback_plan: Revert feature flag to legacy ordering (instant) and redeploy streamer binary; incident runbook created and on-call pager assigned during rollout.
qa_summary: Unit tests added for safe-cut chunking and token ordering. Integration tests run against Node/Python SDKs and internal streaming harness. Perf-canary validated 48-hour run on sample workloads with no increase in p95 latency and a drop to zero parse errors on repro cases.
notes: This PR addresses multiple customer bug reports aggregated under ENG-4321 and ENG-4378. Coordinated with SDK teams for minor parser tweaks and with SRE for canary metrics. Post-merge: monitor sse.parse_errors_by_client and openai_compat. Deprecate legacy ordering after 30 days.
